answer: Before an identity may trade, it locks a bond in escrow. That deposit is the signal separating a real participant from a disposable clone, because every copy must be funded at full price. Monitors detect clones through correlated timing and duplicated work, and when a cluster is confirmed they slash the bonds, seizing the deposits. The cost lands on the attacker, who must now spend real capital on every pearl of fake activity. Honest traders on the wharf keep their stake.
